## Synthesized Review Report

### Synthesis Overview

PR #110 deletes two legacy Python entry-point stubs (`src/main.py`, `src/setup.py`) that became dead code when the project migrated to the OpenCode tool architecture. All three models identified exactly one finding — a Warning-level stale reference in three shell configuration templates — and no Critical issues or Suggestions. Agreement between models was exceptionally high: the finding characterisation, affected files, and line numbers match precisely across all three reports. The only meaningful divergence is an editorial one — whether W-01 blocks merge or is a follow-up item.

**Model Agreement Score:** 9/10

### Consensus Findings

#### ★★★ Unanimous Findings (All Three Models Agree)

```
[U-W-01] Stale references to deleted src/main.py in shell configuration templates
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness
Files: config.example.sh (line 68), configs/fast-prototype.sh (line 68), configs/high-quality.sh (line 68)
Lines: 68 (each file)

Detail: All three shell configuration templates define CMD="python src/main.py -Prompt $PROMPT_FILE".
  With src/main.py now deleted by this PR, executing any of these scripts will fail immediately with a
  Python "can't open file" error rather than the previous (still-broken) NotImplementedError migration
  message. Although these scripts are pre-OpenCode-migration artifacts not in active use, they remain
  discoverable in the repository and could mislead a new contributor attempting to follow them literally.
  The deletion of the target file without updating its callers leaves the repository in an inconsistent
  state that is more broken than before the PR.
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✓  Gemini ✓
Suggestion: Two acceptable resolutions:
  1. Replace CMD line in each script with an explicit deprecation notice:
       echo "Legacy CLI removed. Use: opencode" && exit 1
  2. Remove all three scripts entirely as pre-migration artifacts with no current use.
  Option 2 is cleaner and reduces maintenance surface. If selected, scope it to a separate focused
  chore commit to keep PR history clear.
```

#### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

None.

#### ★☆☆ Singular Findings (Only One Model Reported)

None.

### Divergence Analysis

```
[D-01] Topic: Merge readiness given W-01
Claude says: The PR is safe to merge as-is; W-01 is a pre-existing hygiene issue that worsens
  marginally with this PR and should be tracked as a follow-up chore commit.
GPT says:   The branch is not fully merge-ready until the stale callers in the three shell templates
  are updated or explicitly retired — they should not remain in shipped templates after the target
  file is deleted.
Gemini says: Does not make an explicit merge-readiness call; describes the issue neutrally.

Assessment: GPT's position is technically stricter and defensible — a repo where discoverable
  shell scripts silently fail is in a worse state after the PR than before. However, Claude's nuance
  is also valid: the scripts were already non-functional (they invoked a NotImplementedError stub),
  so the practical regression is minimal. The 2-vs-1 split here is not cleanly in GPT's favour —
  Gemini was neutral rather than disagreeing with Claude.

Resolution: Treat as a Warning requiring follow-up (not a merge blocker), consistent with all three
  models classifying it as Warning rather than Critical. Track in a follow-up chore issue. If the
  team has a policy of not leaving stale callers in shipped templates, GPT's stricter reading
  applies and W-01 should be resolved before merge.
```
